This research project combines the valorization of secondary raw materials derived from the olive supply chain with insect-mediated bioconversion techniques that are sustainable for the local environment. item.title: Contratto di ricerca: THE PERCEPTION OF SOCIOECONOMIC AND TOURISTIC DAMAGE CAUSED BY MACROPLASTICS IN MOUNTAIN ENVIRONMENTS: A CASE STUDY IN THE MOLISE REGION (Univ. MOLISE)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-30 23:59
Institution: Univ. MOLISE, Roma
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-01 Economia agraria, alimentare ed estimo rurale

The research program aims to analyze the perception of the socioeconomic damage caused by waste—macroplastics—in mountain environments by various stakeholders in the context under study (Alto Molise), and the factors that can stimulate "virtuous" behavior. Furthermore, it aims to investigate knowledge of the phenomena, attitudes, and behaviors related to the waste problem in mountain contexts to measure the perception of damage. The study will also assess opinions on the impact that the presence of plastic waste can have on tourism. The types of perceived impact will refer to the landscape, socioeconomic, and tourism damages that the presence of plastic can cause. The program includes…

The project studies how markets can address environmental challenges amid information frictions and behavioral biases. It combines environmental and behavioral economics, field experiments on carbon offsets and air pollution, surveys, and administrative data to assess interventions and welfare effects. It also examines how artificial intelligence can help evaluate environmental claims. The postdoctoral researcher will join an ERC-funded team at Bocconi University and work with the Principal Investigator.
